newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases further against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases further against dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling eased further against the dollar as demand for the currency outstripped supply, commercial bank dealers said on Wednesday.
Against the dollar, the Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.60 compared to 54.51 while against the pound, it was posted at a mean of 90.58 from 90.81.
"We're seeing a very poor supply of dollars from the usual (coffee and tea) exporters," one dealer said.
They added that they expected the shilling to fall further against the dollar, this being a low coffee and tourism season.

Another dealer added that active interbank trading by dealers caught in short dollar positions had helped the shilling breach the 54.75 resistance level and was now looking at 55 as the next psychological level.
"A lot of them were caught offguard because they had positioned themselves for inflows from coffee," one dealer said.
The money market was tight. Overnight rates were quoted at 23 percent
